summary: Iteration 5 — verified 5-plan structure (basic/pro/diamond/golden/business) replacing previous 3-plan free/pro/enterprise. 78/80 backend tests passing. 2 failures expose a real backend bug: _activate_paypal_subscription uses a hardcoded 30-day fallback instead of plan-specific duration_days when next_billing_time is missing, so diamond and business webhook activations get a 30-day expiry instead of 90/365. All other claims in the review request verified (GET /api/plans shape, Stripe checkout for all 5 plans + recurring interval persistence, 400 for enterprise/free/foo, demo user='pro', admin='business' [migration confirmed], PayPal 503 for all 5 plans, max_activations correctly set to 4 [diamond] / 18 [business], payment_provider='paypal' on license, regression auth/license/stats/coupon all green). Frontend Landing /#pricing renders 2-2-1 grid (BASIC gray, PRO blue, DIAMOND purple+MOST POPULAR, GOLDEN orange, BUSINESS green centered) — matches screenshot spec. Dashboard Billing page shows CURRENT PLAN on PRO + 4 SELECT buttons + 4 'OR PAY WITH PAYPAL' secondary buttons.

critical.issue: Hardcoded 30-day fallback for license expires_at when billing_info.next_billing_time is missing. server.py line ~1191: 'period_end = now_utc() + timedelta(days=30)'. For diamond/golden/business this gives a wrong expiry (should be 90/180/365). Fix: replace with cfg.get('duration_days', 30) — same pattern Stripe's _activate_subscription already uses correctly on line 965.

minor.issue: CheckoutIn.plan docstring still says '"pro" | "enterprise"' (server.py line 818). Plan names changed but the inline comment was not updated. Same on PayPalSubscribeIn line 1095.

rca of the issue: Bug: PayPal webhook activation expiry is hardcoded 30 days. Reproduction: POST /api/webhook/paypal with event_type=BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED and resource without billing_info.next_billing_time, custom_id='<user_id>|diamond' → license.expires_at is set to now+30d instead of now+90d. Same for golden (now+30d vs +180d) and business (now+30d vs +365d). Root cause: server.py _activate_paypal_subscription falls back to a literal `timedelta(days=30)` instead of using `cfg.get('duration_days', 30)` like the Stripe counterpart does. Mitigation: one-line change in server.py (~line 1191). After fix, both new test_paypal_webhook_activates_correct_plan parametrize cases will pass, bringing the suite to 80/80.
